title: A freight broker daily routine that protects service and sales.
seoTitle: A freight broker daily routine that protects service and sales
searchIntent: How should a freight broker organize daily tasks and weekly priorities?
excerpt: Sequence active loads, coverage, follow-up, prospecting, and administration without letting a time block override shipment needs.
takeaway: Protect sales time while keeping active shipments visible. Use a routine to organize attention, not to ignore exceptions.

sections.title: Check the moving freight first.
paragraphs: Luis’s daily-routine lessons begin with active loads and customer service. Review pickups, deliveries, carrier status, appointment risks, and the information customers need. Before beginning a new prospecting session, understand what is already moving and what needs intervention.

This first review is not the only shipment check of the day. It establishes the operating picture. A delay or missing detail can change the rest of the plan, so the routine must allow the broker to act when a shipment requires attention.

sections.title: Work pending coverage without waiting passively.
paragraphs: After reviewing active moves, address freight that still needs a carrier. Luis notes that coverage is not always a perfectly linear task. You may send requests or post an opportunity, continue other work, and return when a carrier responds.

The useful distinction is between managing the pending task and staring at it. Keep the shipment requirements and current status visible so you can resume efficiently. A response still needs evaluation; a ringing phone is not proof that the load has been responsibly covered.

sections.title: Follow up before starting from zero.
paragraphs: The lessons prioritize people who have already engaged: previous conversations, quote requests, and agreed follow-ups. Those contacts have context that should shape the next exchange. Work from the record rather than giving the same first-call introduction each time.

Cold prospecting follows as a separate activity. Luis prefers later-morning contact after shipping managers have handled their initial operations, but that is his practice rather than universal research on the best calling time. Match your activity to the people and business you are trying to reach.

sections.title: Recheck shipments while protecting focused work.
paragraphs: The time-blocking lesson organizes attention into active-load service, sales, another tracking and administrative period, and preparation for the next day. The daily-routine lesson makes clear that service remains active during sales work. After a period of outreach, recheck the loads and respond to changes.

An urgent shipment exception overrides the calendar. The schedule is valuable because it prevents routine work from consuming every available hour by default. It is not a rule that customer communication must wait until the next scheduled block.

sections.title: Close the day with documents and tomorrow’s priorities.
paragraphs: Later-day work in the lesson includes payables, receivables, invoices, carrier questions, and shipment documents. Giving those tasks a place in the routine reduces the temptation to leave them indefinitely because another sales activity feels more urgent.

Prepare the next prospect list and priorities outside the time you intend to use for contact. The next session should begin with usable work rather than another decision about where to start. Luis also emphasizes a stopping point and recovery time instead of treating continuous availability as the only way to operate.

sections.title: Add a weekly review above the daily routine.
paragraphs: The weekly-priorities lesson asks brokers to review customers whose load activity has fallen. A reduction could reflect seasonality, a service problem, or lost share; ask rather than assume. It also includes professional-network development, consistent follow-up, and individual agent check-ins.

Discuss the accounts being pursued, quote responsiveness, wins, losses, and support needed. This review connects daily activity to the condition of the business. It helps reveal whether the routine is protecting the right work or simply keeping everyone occupied.
